Night radio checks rules
This page walks new staff through how a new handler works

The Companion Animal Travel Desk keeps pet travel steady, gentle, and predictable, so every handoff feels safe for the animal and clear for the traveler. When you start a shift, think comfort first and speed second. We want each person, crate, leash, and document to move in a calm flow, because animals read our energy quickly and travelers trust us to set the tone.

A new handler begins by greeting the traveler in a relaxed way, then looking over the booking details, crate setup, and pet condition before anything moves forward. Speak plainly, keep your voice soft, and never crowd the animal. If a pet seems nervous, slow the pace, lower the noise around the desk, and give the traveler simple guidance on what will happen next. This is also the moment to notice anything unusual about the animal's appearance or behavior and share it through the proper channel without delay. <<FACT F102>>

Next, check that the traveler has the right paperwork ready and that the details match the reservation. <<FACT F086>> Read names, pet descriptions, and travel notes with care, because small mismatches can cause a bigger delay later. If anything is unclear, pause the handoff and ask for the missing detail before the animal is accepted. Keep the language friendly and steady, since a worried traveler usually settles down when the process feels organized.

For the actual check-in, stay focused on humane handling. Use the crate and leash rules exactly as trained, and never rush a pet into a space that feels too tight or too loud. Give the traveler short updates as you work, and make sure they understand where to wait and how they will be guided next. The best service here is quiet confidence, not fast movement.

When the handoff is finished, confirm that all notes are complete and that any concern has been passed along clearly. What to remember is simple: calm handling, clean communication, and careful checking protect both the pet and the journey.
